calls.head: The Sharks give up shots, and the Kings take them
calls.body: San Jose has been giving up shots all season, and the Kings rarely pass one up.
calls.call: The Kings take at least their usual 59.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Los Angeles 8th for shot volume (59.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · San Jose 23rd for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Los Angeles took 61.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 59.9.

calls.head: The Sharks hunt better looks than the Kings
calls.body: The Sharks are around the middle of the league for shot quality, at the dangerous end; the Kings are the league’s worst, at the hopeful end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Sharks’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Kings’.
calls.nums: Shot quality: San Jose 14th, Los Angeles 32nd
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot was, San Jose had 4.0% a shot and Los Angeles 6.7% a shot. Coming in, San Jose was at 6.3% a shot and Los Angeles at 5.7% a shot.
calls.usual: SJS 6.3% a shot · LAK 5.7% a shot
calls.tonight: SJS 4.0% a shot · LAK 6.7% a shot

SJS.head: We had this close to even (49% for San Jose), and San Jose came through.

LAK.head: We had this close to even (51% for Los Angeles), and it went San Jose’s way.

surprises.head: San Jose won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, Los Angeles wins 83. San Jose won anyway.

surprises.head: San Jose couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 50 games.
surprises.flipped: The Sharks hunt better looks than the Kings

surprises.head: A rough night for A. Forsberg
surprises.body: A. Forsberg allowed 5 goals on shots worth 1.7 expected goals, 3.3 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 45 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: The Sharks steal one
paras: Adrian Kempe opened the scoring late in the first. Igor Chernyshov added two goals. Four different Sharks scored. The game was tied twice. Chernyshov won it in overtime.
The Kings had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Kings win about four in five. By our Swing measure, Artemi Panarin had the best night of anyone, even in a loss.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
